about.title: Half Moon Bay Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Half Moon Bay's coastal location along Highway 1 means many residents rely on urgent care clinics, small medical practices, or facilities in nearby San Mateo or Redwood City for anything beyond routine care. When that care falls short of accepted medical standards, patients can be left with lasting harm that goes well beyond a simple bad outcome. California law recognizes this distinction and gives injured patients a path to hold providers accountable through a medical malpractice claim. Because these cases involve strict notice requirements, filing deadlines, and the near-universal need for a qualified medical expert to review the care given, having someone who understands the process matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge any fee to connect you. We simply link Half Moon Bay residents who believe they were harmed by a medical error with an independent attorney who can evaluate the specifics of what happened and explain the options available under California's malpractice statutes.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You File

items.title: Strict Notice and Filing Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires a claim within one year of discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider before a lawsuit can be filed.

items.title: A Medical Expert Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, California cases nearly always need a qualified medical expert to show the care fell below the accepted standard.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises
items.desc: State law places a cap on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap increases each year under MICRA, which an attorney can explain as it applies to your situation.

items.question: I live in Half Moon Bay but was treated at a hospital outside the city — can I still get help?
items.answer: Yes. Medical malpractice claims are based on where the care was provided and where you live isn't a barrier to pursuing a claim. Many Half Moon Bay residents receive treatment at facilities in San Mateo County or beyond, and an independent attorney can look into a claim regardless of which facility was involved.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice to the provider before filing suit, so timing matters and it's worth having a claim reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result by itself isn't proof of malpractice; the care given has to have fallen below the accepted medical standard. That's why a qualified medical expert almost always needs to review the case, which is something an independent attorney can help arrange.
